newsitem.title: GERMANY: Steffi Graf father says tax accusations inflated.
newsitem.headline: Steffi Graf father says tax accusations inflated.

text.p: Lawyers for tennis star Steffi Graf's father on Friday told a court trying him for tax dodging that he had evaded at most five million marks ($3.3 million), not the 19 million marks prosecutors allege.
Peter Graf is accused, together with family advisor Joachim Eckardt, of funnelling abroad 42 million marks of the world number one's earnings between 1989 and 1993.

But tax lawyer Berthold Wipfler told the court that the question of which income should have been taxed abroad and which in Germany was a matter of debate. He said not all the player's advertising contracts were liable for tax in Germany.
"As far as we are concerned there is a tax debt of no more than five milliion marks," he said.
Eckardt's lawyer Bernd Schneider said prosecutors had "worked on the principle that the tax authorities always get the benefit of the doubt".
But senior prosecutor Hubert Jobski dismissed this idea.
"This is a court and not a weekend seminar on how to minimise your tax payments," he retorted.
Peter Graf, 58, has been in detention since August last year and went on trial in Mannheim earlier this month. He could face a maximum sentence of 10 years.

Known to sponsors for collecting money in cash in plastic bags, he said earlier in the proceedings that authorities signalled their approval of his tax schemes to prevent his daughter joining an exodus of German sporting tax exiles.
Steffi Graf herself remains under investigation, although she says she left her financial affairs to her father from an early age and did not even know how much money she was making.
The U.S. Open champion is due to appear before a home crowd at the $430,000 Leipzig tournament next week.
